notes: `יִשָּׂא פְּנֵי` → *regard* writes neither morpheme's lexeme, so rule 6's deterministic first-token anchor governs the indivisible pair.
כָל standing on the noun is itself what *any* renders, so the noun keeps only its own word (rule 15).

The competing reading heads the *thou givest many* unit on *givest*; רבה is the multiplying, so the lexeme sits in *many* and rule 56's auxiliary-verb clause does not reach it, no second Hebrew verb standing in the clause (rules 31, 44).
